method: Chat messages sent by hand in the ScanBorn app; timings are the app's own onStats JNI callback, read from adb logcat. Each run is a single measurement and phone temperature was not controlled. The baseline run used a slightly shorter prompt; every later run used the same 359-token prompt. The two repack runs are a same-binary A/B: one installed build, only debug.scanborn.repack differed.

model.name: qwen2.5-1.5b-instruct
model.repack_eligible_note: Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K matmul weights with ne[1] % 8 == 0, excluding token_embd.weight (125.2 MiB); computed from the GGUF tensor table and matched by the device log

builds.baseline: MOBILE-APP debug, built 2026-09-14 00:27. -O3, no -march/-mcpu, so ggml's dotprod and i8mm kernels are compiled out.
builds.arm_optimised: MOBILE-APP debug, built 2026-09-14 02:50. ggml_cpu compiled with -march=armv8.2-a+dotprod+i8mm; libscanborn_jni.so contains 209 sdot and 36 smmla instructions. scanborn_jni.cpp stays baseline and checks HWCAP_ASIMDDP and HWCAP2_I8MM before loading.
builds.arm_optimised_repack: MOBILE-APP debug, built 2026-09-14 04:15. As arm_optimised, plus GGML_USE_CPU_REPACK on ggml_cpu. scanborn_jni.cpp sets use_extra_bufts from debug.scanborn.repack (unset = on, "0" = off), so both modes run from one binary.

startup.note: model_load_ms after the first load benefits from a warm page cache, so load times are not a clean build comparison; the two repack launches were back to back

memory_kb.note: From /proc/<pid>/status and dumpsys meminfo on the arm_optimised_repack build. rss_anon is app-owned memory Android cannot reclaim (only compress to zram swap); rss_file is model-file pages Android can drop under pressure.

runs.thread_source: adb shell setprop debug.scanborn.threads 4 (confirmed by 'threads overridden' in the load log)

runs.repack_source: adb shell setprop debug.scanborn.repack 0 (confirmed by 'weight repacking: off' in the load log)

conclusions: ARM-optimised vs baseline at 6 threads: decode about +32%, prefill about +18%, total time about -18%.
4 vs 6 threads on the ARM-optimised build: prefill about +5%, decode about -12%, total about +6%. 6 threads remains the default.

Same-binary A/B, repack on vs off at 6 threads: prefill +47% (69.0 vs 46.8 tok/s), first token 31% sooner (5.3 vs 7.7 s), total 26% shorter (19.0 vs 25.7 s). Model load is slower with repack (2.8 vs 2.1 s).
Repack moves the eligible weights (934 MiB) out of the reclaimable model file into app-owned memory: after a reply, total PSS is about the same (1.35 vs 1.33 GiB) but rss_anon is 1.15 vs 0.28 GiB.

Decode ranged from 14.2 to 19.1 tok/s across runs of the same prompt with the same decode kernels, so decode differences of this size are within run-to-run noise here. Prefill without repacking stayed at 41-47 tok/s; 69 tok/s with repacking is well outside that range.
Repacking is on by default in the build; debug.scanborn.repack=0 turns it off for the next model load.
